short: The first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, serving over fifty years in the US Navy.
full:
Commissioned on 25 November 1961, USS Enterprise (CVN-65) was the world's first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier. Powered by eight nuclear reactors, it represented a massive leap in naval engineering, boasting essentially unlimited range and the ability to sustain high speeds indefinitely. Its early years saw it participate in the blockade during the Cuban Missile Crisis and undertake multiple combat deployments during the Vietnam War.

The Enterprise proved the viability and immense strategic advantage of nuclear power for surface combatants, leading directly to the development of all subsequent American supercarriers. Serving for over fifty years, it became the longest-serving aircraft carrier in United States Navy history. It was inactivated in 2012 and officially decommissioned on 3 February 2017, having participated in nearly every major American naval operation of the Cold War and beyond.
